definitions.explanation: Describes someone who lacks skill or ability in something. The opposite of {上手|じょうず} (skillful). Can be self-deprecating when used about oneself.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}は{歌|うた}が{下手|へた}です。
{字|じ}が{下手|へた}ですみません。
{下手|へた}でもいいから、{挑戦|ちょうせん}しよう。
examples.english: Even if I'm not good at it, let's give it a try.

notes: The opposite of {上手|じょうず}. Uses the same grammar pattern: ～が{下手|へた}です (bad at ~). It's considered polite in Japanese to be modest about your own abilities, so saying {下手|へた}です about yourself is common and not necessarily negative. Avoid using it directly about others as it can be rude.
